newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino kidnap victims freed after 34 days.
newsitem.headline: Filipino kidnap victims freed after 34 days.

text.p: Moslem guerillas on Friday freed unharmed two government employees from 34 days of captivity in the southern Philippines after officials promised to consider amnesty for the kidnappers.

Presidential Executive Secretary Ruben Torres said that Moslem regional governor Nur Misuari, head of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) which signed a peace deal with the government last year, negotiated the release of the two employees of the Philippine National Oil Co (PNOC).

Torres told reporters no ransom was paid but the government, aside from the amnesty promise, also pledged to provide livelihood to the members of the kidnap gang and develop the swampy area where they live.
Asked why the government would give them amnesty, Torres said, "They are rebels, in fact former members of the MNLF and so we are looking into the amnesty."
"There might be legal problems and so we are trying to work this out. This is the only way we can get them back to the folds of the law," Torres added.
The two were among five PNOC employees who were abducted at gunpoint on January 19 while on their way to conduct geological surveys in Maguindanao province.
The kidnappers had demanded a ransom of five million pesos ($192,000) for the group but released three of them after more than a week.
